first.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious move, but it is also the action most likely to trade long-term qualified revenue for short-term acquisition, and memory_73 is the inherited claim I trust least: it is unusually broad and self-reinforcing for a single archived record (acquisition lift AND revenue lift AND time-to-first-value AND holding across both billing plans). Claims that sweeping usually indicate summary drift across consolidations rather than a genuinely multi-outcome result, so it gets one verification slot. If the source record turns out to show a narrow, discount-driven acquisition bump with no retention or margin follow-up, matching a price cut against a better-funded competitor would likely erode the exact metric the objective names.

The second slot goes to memory_31 because it is the oldest inherited memory (day 12, now 64 days stale) and it carries the load-bearing word 'durable' for the direction I currently intend. I want to know whether 'durable' was measured over a real window or asserted at the end of a short test.

My current intent is simplify_onboarding. Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%; onboarding plausibly sits upstream of activation, so repairing the funnel entrance may recover part of both, whereas activation_messaging (memory_91) treats the downstream symptom. Two independent inherited records (memory_86, memory_31) point the same way, which is weak but real convergent support. This is also the lowest-regret option: it does not set a discount precedent, does not spend referral goodwill, and does not commit sales capacity.

Uncertainty I am explicitly not resolving away: I do not know that the onboarding decline causes the activation decline rather than both sharing an external cause, such as a shift in inbound traffic mix driven by the competitor. Nor do I know that day-12 and day-52 onboarding findings still hold on today's traffic. I am running standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout for that reason, and I would drop to small_guarded_test if memory_31 verifies weakly. Downstream value risk is flagged for both the discount path (acquiring price-shopping accounts that depress retention and margin while inflating headline revenue) and for the intended path (removing signup fields can raise activation counts while lowering lead quality, so qualified-revenue metrics must be tracked, not just activation rate). enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) stays open as the fallback if verification undermines the self-serve funnel thesis, since it targets pipeline quality directly.
